title: One Hand Holds
logline: In a small moonstone workshop, a cutter grips a rough stone firmly in one hand while the other, for hours, does nothing but polish.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: After the loud, public effort of a kite launch, wanting-to-do turns quiet and private in the southern low country: one hand polishing a stone for hours with no one watching.

thread_out.thread: Patient effort that expects a result gives way to its opposite: a daily ritual of buying the same numbers, wanting without quite expecting.

requirements: A working lapidary or goldsmith's workshop
A cutter willing to be filmed over the span of one piece's completion

lesson.in_simple_terms: Some effort is quiet: one hand holding steady while the other works, hour after hour, with no one watching. The feeling that comes with it need not be excitement; it can be neither pleasant nor unpleasant.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කිසිවෙකු නොබලා සිටියදීත් එක් අතකින් ගල තදින් අල්ලාගෙන අනෙක් අතින් පැය ගණන් ඔප දැමීම නිහඬ උත්සාහයක් වන අතර, එයට එක්වන හැඟීම සතුටක් හෝ දුකක් නොව මැදහත් වේදනාවක් විය හැකිය.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma's image for sustained application (vicāra) is a hand gripping a metal pot firmly while the other hand slowly polishes it: the mind staying with its object and working over it. Effort (vīriya) is described as the mental quality that does not turn back from a task until it is done, and explicitly not as bodily strength. The compendium of feeling says every moment carries a feeling, and counts neutral feeling (upekkhā), neither pleasant nor painful, in fifty-five kinds of mind, from ordinary ones to the most refined.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Long, nearly still shots of the cutter, one hand gripping the stone while the other polishes, let the viewer feel how the work holds attention without drama. Checks under the lens and the slow change from dull to shining mark progress that no one applauds, and the absence of excitement in the room lets the viewer notice a feeling that is neither joy nor strain.
lesson.caution: This does not mean that hard work is always virtuous or that neutral feeling is numbness: the texts say effort can serve harm as easily as good, and they find neutral feeling in both ordinary and the most refined minds.
lesson.builds_on: The last film contrasted the effortful launch with the steady glide; this one stays entirely with the steady holding, and adds that such effort can come with quiet, neutral feeling rather than excitement.
